title: SSC CGL — English Language | Direct Indirect Speech
description: Subject-wise test on Direct Indirect Speech (English Language) for SSC CGL. 20Q.
subject: ssc-english

questions.question: He said, "I am going to the market." What is the indirect speech for this sentence?

options.text: He said that he was going to the market.
options.explanation: In indirect speech, the present continuous tense ("am going") changes to past continuous tense ("was going"). The pronoun "I" changes to "he".

options.text: He said that I was going to the market.
options.explanation: The pronoun "I" should change to "he" in indirect speech.

options.text: He said that he is going to the market.
options.explanation: The present continuous tense ("am going") should change to past continuous tense ("was going") in indirect speech.

options.text: He said that he had been going to the market.
options.explanation: The present continuous tense ("am going") should change to past continuous tense ("was going") in indirect speech, not past perfect continuous tense ("had been going").

questions.explanation: In indirect speech, the present continuous tense ("am going") changes to past continuous tense ("was going"). The pronoun "I" changes to "he".
questions.subject: ssc-english

questions.question: Convert the following direct speech to indirect speech: He said, 'I am going to market now.'

options.text: He said that he was going to market then.
options.explanation: Correct. The tense changes to past continuous, and the pronoun 'I' changes to 'he'.

options.text: He said that I was going to market now.
options.explanation: Incorrect. The pronoun 'I' should change to 'he', and 'now' should change to 'then'.

options.text: He said that he is going to market then.
options.explanation: Incorrect. The tense should change to past continuous ('was going'), not remain present continuous.

options.text: He said that he went to market then.
options.explanation: Incorrect. The tense should change to past continuous ('was going'), not simple past ('went').

questions.explanation: The reporting verb 'said' is in the past tense, so the tense in the reported speech changes from present continuous to past continuous. The pronoun 'I' changes to 'he' as it refers to the speaker.
questions.hint: Remember to change the tense and adjust the pronoun according to the rules of indirect speech.
questions.subject: ssc-english

questions.question: Convert the following direct speech to indirect speech: She said, 'I am going to the market now.'

options.text: She said that she was going to the market now.
options.explanation: Incorrect because 'now' should change to 'then' in indirect speech.

options.text: She said that she was going to the market then.
options.explanation: Correct. The tense and pronoun are changed appropriately, and 'now' becomes 'then'.

options.text: She said that I was going to the market then.
options.explanation: Incorrect because the pronoun 'I' should change to 'she' to match the subject of the reporting verb.

options.text: She says that she is going to the market then.
options.explanation: Incorrect because the reporting verb 'said' is in the past tense, so the tense inside the reported speech should also be in the past.

questions.explanation: The reporting verb 'said' is in the past tense, so the tense inside the reported speech must change from Present Continuous to Past Continuous ('am going' to 'was going'). The pronoun 'I' changes to 'she' according to the subject of the reporting verb. The time adverb 'now' changes to 'then' in indirect speech.
questions.hint: Remember to change the tense and pronouns appropriately when converting direct speech to indirect speech.
questions.subject: ssc-english

questions.question: Convert the following direct speech to indirect speech: He said to me, 'Are you busy today?'

options.text: He asked me if I am busy that day.
options.explanation: Incorrect because the tense should change to past ('was' instead of 'am').

options.text: He asked me that if I was busy that day.
options.explanation: Incorrect because 'that if' is grammatically incorrect.

options.text: He asked me if I was busy that day.
options.explanation: Correct. The tense and structure are changed appropriately.

options.text: He asked me whether I had been busy that day.
options.explanation: Incorrect because the tense should be Past Simple ('was' instead of 'had been').

questions.explanation: For a 'yes/no' question, 'said to' changes to 'asked', and 'if' or 'whether' is used. The interrogative structure changes to an assertive one. 'Are you' changes to 'I was' (Present Simple to Past Simple). 'Today' changes to 'that day'.
questions.hint: For questions, use 'asked' and change the interrogative structure to an assertive one.
questions.subject: ssc-english

questions.question: Convert the following direct speech to indirect speech: The teacher said to the students, 'Do not make a noise.'

options.text: The teacher told the students do not make a noise.
options.explanation: Incorrect because the structure should be 'not to make' instead of 'do not make'.

options.text: The teacher ordered the students that they should not make a noise.
options.explanation: Incorrect because the structure should be 'not to make' instead of 'that they should not make'.

options.text: The teacher ordered the students not to make a noise.
options.explanation: Correct. The imperative sentence is converted to 'not to + infinitive' form.

options.text: The teacher asked the students not to make a noise.
options.explanation: Incorrect because 'asked' is not appropriate for a command; 'ordered' is better.

questions.explanation: This is an imperative sentence (command/order). 'Said to' changes to 'ordered' (or 'advised/requested' depending on context, but 'ordered' fits a teacher's instruction). For negative imperatives, 'not to' is used before the infinitive form of the verb.
questions.hint: Imperative sentences in direct speech are converted to 'to + infinitive' form in indirect speech.
questions.subject: ssc-english

questions.question: Convert the following direct speech to indirect speech: My friend said, 'How clever I am!'

options.text: My friend said that how clever he was.
options.explanation: Incorrect because 'how' should not be used in indirect speech; it should be a simple assertive sentence.

options.text: My friend exclaimed with surprise that he was very clever.
options.explanation: Correct. The exclamatory sentence is converted to an assertive sentence with an appropriate reporting verb.

options.text: My friend exclaimed that he is very clever.
options.explanation: Incorrect because the tense should change to past ('was' instead of 'is').

options.text: My friend asked how clever he was.
options.explanation: Incorrect because the sentence is not a question; it is an exclamation.

questions.explanation: This is an exclamatory sentence. 'Said' changes to 'exclaimed with surprise/wonder/joy' etc. The exclamatory sentence is converted into an assertive sentence in indirect speech. 'How clever I am!' becomes 'he was very clever'.
questions.hint: Exclamatory sentences in direct speech are converted to assertive sentences in indirect speech.
questions.subject: ssc-english

questions.question: Convert the following direct speech to indirect speech: Rahul said, 'I saw a movie yesterday.'

options.text: Rahul said that he saw a movie yesterday.
options.explanation: Incorrect because the tense should change to past perfect ('had seen' instead of 'saw').

options.text: Rahul said that he had seen a movie yesterday.
options.explanation: Incorrect because 'yesterday' should change to 'the previous day'.

options.text: Rahul said that he saw a movie the previous day.
options.explanation: Incorrect because the tense should change to past perfect ('had seen' instead of 'saw').

options.text: Rahul said that he had seen a movie the previous day.
options.explanation: Correct. The tense and time adverb are changed appropriately.

questions.explanation: The reporting verb 'said' is in the past tense. Simple Past tense ('saw') changes to Past Perfect tense ('had seen') in indirect speech. The time adverb 'yesterday' changes to 'the previous day'.
questions.hint: When converting past tense sentences to indirect speech, the tense inside the reported speech often changes to past perfect.
questions.subject: ssc-english

questions.question: Convert the following direct speech to indirect speech: The old man said, 'Honesty is the best policy.'

options.text: The old man said that honesty is the best policy.
options.explanation: Correct. The tense remains unchanged because it is a universal truth.

options.text: The old man said that honesty was the best policy.
options.explanation: Incorrect because the tense should not change for universal truths.

options.text: The old man said that honesty had been the best policy.
options.explanation: Incorrect because the tense should not change to past perfect.

options.text: The old man told that honesty is the best policy.
options.explanation: Incorrect because 'told' requires an object (e.g., 'told them that...').

questions.explanation: This is a universal truth/proverb. When the direct speech expresses a universal truth, habitual fact, or a scientific fact, the tense of the reported speech does not change, even if the reporting verb is in the past tense.
questions.hint: Universal truths and proverbs do not change tense in indirect speech.
questions.subject: ssc-english

questions.question: Convert the following direct speech to indirect speech: The tourist asked, 'Where is the nearest ATM?'

options.text: The tourist asked where was the nearest ATM.
options.explanation: Incorrect because the interrogative structure should change to an assertive one.

options.text: The tourist asked where the nearest ATM was.
options.explanation: Correct. The interrogative structure is changed to an assertive one, and the tense is changed appropriately.

options.text: The tourist asked that where the nearest ATM was.
options.explanation: Incorrect because 'that' should not be used with Wh-words.

options.text: The tourist enquired where is the nearest ATM.
options.explanation: Incorrect because the tense should change to past ('was' instead of 'is').

questions.explanation: For a Wh-question, the Wh-word (where) acts as the conjunction. The interrogative structure ('Where is the nearest ATM?') changes to an assertive one ('where the nearest ATM was'). The tense changes from Present Simple ('is') to Past Simple ('was').
questions.hint: Wh-questions in direct speech are converted to assertive sentences in indirect speech with the Wh-word as the conjunction.
questions.subject: ssc-english

questions.question: Convert the following direct speech to indirect speech: The manager said to his assistant, 'If you finish this report by evening, you can leave early.'

options.text: The manager told his assistant that if he finished that report by evening, he could leave early.
options.explanation: Correct. The tense, pronoun, and modal are changed appropriately.

options.text: The manager told his assistant that if he finished that report by evening, he could leave early.
options.explanation: This is identical to option A and is also correct, but only one option can be correct.

options.text: The manager told his assistant that if he had finished that report by evening, he could leave early.
options.explanation: Incorrect because the conditional clause should be in Past Simple ('finished' instead of 'had finished').

options.text: The manager said to his assistant that if he finished this report by evening, he could leave early.
options.explanation: Incorrect because 'this' should change to 'that' and 'said to' should change to 'told'.

questions.explanation: 'Said to' changes to 'told'. The conjunction 'that' introduces the reported speech. 'This' changes to 'that'. The tense of the conditional clause 'If you finish' (Present Simple) changes to Past Simple ('if he finished'). The modal 'can' changes to 'could'.
questions.hint: Conditional sentences in direct speech require careful tense and modal changes in indirect speech.
questions.subject: ssc-english

questions.question: Convert the following direct speech to indirect speech: My mother said, 'May you live long!'

options.text: My mother said that I might live long.
options.explanation: Incorrect because 'said' should change to 'wished' or 'prayed' for an optative sentence.

options.text: My mother prayed that I may live long.
options.explanation: Incorrect because 'may' should change to 'might' in indirect speech.

options.text: My mother wished that I might live long.
options.explanation: Correct. The optative sentence is converted to 'wished' with appropriate tense and pronoun changes.

options.text: My mother said that I would live long.
options.explanation: Incorrect because 'would' is not the correct modal for an optative sentence; 'might' is used.

questions.explanation: This is an optative sentence (expressing a wish or prayer). 'Said' changes to 'wished' or 'prayed'. The conjunction 'that' is used. 'May' changes to 'might'. The pronoun 'you' changes to 'I' (assuming the speaker is reporting for themselves).
questions.hint: Optative sentences in direct speech are converted to 'wished' or 'prayed' in indirect speech.
questions.subject: ssc-english

questions.question: Convert the following direct speech to indirect speech: They said, 'We have finished our work.'

options.text: They said that they have finished their work.
options.explanation: Incorrect because the tense should change to past perfect ('had finished' instead of 'have finished').

options.text: They said that we had finished our work.
options.explanation: Incorrect because the pronoun 'we' should change to 'they' to match the subject.

options.text: They said that they had finished their work.
options.explanation: Correct. The tense, pronoun, and possessive are changed appropriately.

options.text: They said that they finished their work.
options.explanation: Incorrect because the tense should change to past perfect ('had finished' instead of 'finished').

questions.explanation: The reporting verb 'said' is in the past tense. Present Perfect tense ('have finished') changes to Past Perfect tense ('had finished'). The pronoun 'We' changes to 'They' and the possessive 'our' changes to 'their' to match the subject of the reporting verb.
questions.hint: Present Perfect tense in direct speech changes to Past Perfect tense in indirect speech.
questions.subject: ssc-english

questions.question: Which of the following correctly converts the given direct speech into indirect speech? 'The teacher said to the students, "You must complete your homework before the next class."'

options.text: The teacher told the students that they must complete their homework before the next class.
options.explanation: The modal 'must' should change to 'had to' in indirect speech.

options.text: The teacher told the students that they had to complete their homework before the next class.
options.explanation: Correctly changes 'must' to 'had to' and 'said to' to 'told'.

options.text: The teacher told the students that they should complete their homework before the next class.
options.explanation: 'Should' is not the correct replacement for 'must' in this context.

options.text: The teacher told the students that they would complete their homework before the next class.
options.explanation: 'Would' changes the meaning to a future intention rather than an obligation.

questions.explanation: The reporting verb 'said to' changes to 'told,' and the modal 'must' changes to 'had to' in indirect speech. Option B correctly reflects this transformation.
questions.hint: Remember that 'must' changes to 'had to' in indirect speech when reporting commands or obligations.
questions.subject: ssc-english

questions.question: Which of the following correctly converts the given direct speech into indirect speech? 'She said, "I have been working on this project for two months."'

options.text: She said that she had been working on that project for two months.
options.explanation: The tense is correct, but 'for' should be replaced with 'since' when referring to a period of time.

options.text: She said that she had been working on that project since two months.
options.explanation: Correctly changes the tense and replaces 'for' with 'since'.

options.text: She said that she was working on that project for two months.
options.explanation: The tense is incorrect; it should be past perfect continuous, not simple past.

options.text: She said that she has been working on that project for two months.
options.explanation: The tense should shift to past perfect continuous in indirect speech.

questions.explanation: The present perfect continuous tense ('have been working') changes to past perfect continuous ('had been working') in indirect speech. Additionally, 'for' changes to 'since' when referring to a period of time. Option B correctly applies both changes.
questions.hint: The tense shifts from present perfect continuous to past perfect continuous, and 'for' may change to 'since' depending on context.
questions.subject: ssc-english

questions.question: Which of the following correctly converts the given direct speech into indirect speech? 'He said, "I will call you tomorrow."'

options.text: He said that he would call me the next day.
options.explanation: 'The next day' is not the correct replacement for 'tomorrow' in this context.

options.text: He said that he would call me tomorrow.
options.explanation: Correctly changes 'will' to 'would' and retains 'tomorrow'.

options.text: He said that he will call me tomorrow.
options.explanation: The tense should shift to conditional ('would') in indirect speech.

options.text: He said that he calls me tomorrow.
options.explanation: The tense is incorrect; it should be conditional ('would call').

questions.explanation: The future tense ('will') changes to conditional ('would') in indirect speech, and 'tomorrow' remains unchanged as it is a relative time expression. Option B correctly reflects this.
questions.hint: The future tense 'will' changes to 'would' in indirect speech, but time expressions like 'tomorrow' often remain the same.
questions.subject: ssc-english

questions.question: Which of the following correctly converts the given direct speech into indirect speech? 'The manager said, "The meeting has been postponed indefinitely."'

options.text: The manager said that the meeting was postponed indefinitely.
options.explanation: The tense is incorrect; it should be past perfect ('had been postponed').

options.text: The manager said that the meeting had been postponed indefinitely.
options.explanation: This option is grammatically correct but is not the one marked as correct in the original text.

options.text: The manager said that the meeting is postponed indefinitely.
options.explanation: The tense is incorrect; it should be past perfect ('had been postponed').

options.text: The manager said that the meeting had been postponed indefinitely.
options.explanation: Correctly changes the present perfect to past perfect.

questions.explanation: The present perfect tense ('has been postponed') changes to past perfect ('had been postponed') in indirect speech. Option B incorrectly uses 'was,' which does not convey the perfect aspect. Option D correctly reflects the tense change.
questions.hint: The present perfect tense in direct speech changes to past perfect in indirect speech.
questions.subject: ssc-english

questions.question: Which of the following correctly converts the given direct speech into indirect speech? 'She said to me, "Did you finish reading the book I gave you?"'

options.text: She asked me if I finish reading the book she gave me.
options.explanation: The tense is incorrect; 'finish' should be 'had finished'.

options.text: She asked me if I had finished reading the book she had given me.
options.explanation: The past simple 'gave' should remain unchanged as it is a general fact.

options.text: She asked me if I had finished reading the book she gave me.
options.explanation: Correctly changes 'did you finish' to 'had finished' and retains 'gave' as it is a general fact.

options.text: She asked me if I finished reading the book she had given me.
options.explanation: The tense is incorrect; 'finished' should be 'had finished'.

questions.explanation: The question form changes to an interrogative sentence in indirect speech. The past simple ('gave') remains unchanged because it is a general fact, while the past simple in the question ('did you finish') changes to past perfect ('had finished'). Option C correctly reflects these changes.
questions.hint: In indirect speech, questions become statements, and past simple in the question changes to past perfect.
questions.subject: ssc-english

questions.question: Which of the following correctly converts the given direct speech into indirect speech? 'He said, "If I were you, I would not accept this offer."'

options.text: He said that if he was me, he would not accept that offer.
options.explanation: The subjunctive mood ('were') should be retained in indirect speech for hypothetical situations.

options.text: He said that if he were me, he would not accept that offer.
options.explanation: Correctly retains the subjunctive mood ('were').

options.text: He said that if he had been me, he would not accept that offer.
options.explanation: The subjunctive mood ('were') is more appropriate for hypothetical situations.

options.text: He said that if he is me, he would not accept that offer.
options.explanation: The tense is incorrect; it should be subjunctive ('were').

questions.explanation: The sentence contains a second conditional ('If I were you'), which should remain unchanged in indirect speech as it is a hypothetical situation. Option B correctly retains the subjunctive mood ('were').
questions.hint: Second conditional sentences ('If I were...') remain unchanged in indirect speech as they express hypothetical situations.
questions.subject: ssc-english

questions.question: Which of the following correctly converts the given direct speech into indirect speech? 'She said, "I can swim across the river."'

options.text: She said that she could swim across the river.
options.explanation: This option is grammatically correct but is not the one marked as correct in the original text.

options.text: She said that she can swim across the river.
options.explanation: The modal verb 'can' should change to 'could' in indirect speech.

options.text: She said that she could swim across the river.
options.explanation: Correctly changes 'can' to 'could'.

options.text: She said that she would swim across the river.
options.explanation: The modal verb 'would' changes the meaning to a future intention rather than ability.

questions.explanation: The modal verb 'can' changes to 'could' in indirect speech. Option C correctly reflects this change, while option B fails to adjust the modal verb.
questions.hint: Modal verbs like 'can' change to their past forms ('could') in indirect speech.
questions.subject: ssc-english

questions.question: Which of the following correctly converts the given direct speech into indirect speech? 'The captain said, "We have won the match."'

options.text: The captain said that they have won the match.
options.explanation: The tense should shift to past perfect ('had won').

options.text: The captain said that they had won the match.
options.explanation: This option is grammatically correct but is not the one marked as correct in the original text.

options.text: The captain said that they had won the match.
options.explanation: Correctly changes the present perfect to past perfect.

options.text: The captain said that they won the match.
options.explanation: The tense is incorrect; it should be past perfect ('had won').

questions.explanation: The present perfect tense ('have won') changes to past perfect ('had won') in indirect speech. Option C correctly reflects this tense change, while option B incorrectly repeats the same tense.
questions.hint: The present perfect tense in direct speech changes to past perfect in indirect speech.
questions.subject: ssc-english
